name: Cult of Reason
summary: The Cult of Reason was the civic, naturalistic religion that Paris revolutionaries around the Commune promoted from November 1793 to replace Christianity, centring devotion on Reason, Liberty and the Republic in festivals held in churches turned into temples of Reason. The scholarship describes it as a collection of atheistic ideas and practices rather than a unified institution or a coherent system of belief; Robespierre's Cult of the Supreme Being displaced it in 1794. Its recorded content is almost wholly about religion and the Church, so it says little on the economic, social or foreign-policy questions of the test.

scope: The atheistic, civic Cult of Reason of 1793-94 as the New Catholic Encyclopedia, Jaures and Journal18 describe it: the cult of Reason and Liberty proclaimed by the Paris Commune and taken up by local clubs and representatives on mission. It excludes the wider dechristianization campaign and the Hebertist faction's politics (price controls, terror, war policy), the Cult of the Supreme Being, and later religions of humanity or reason.
